title: 349. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Properties of Parallelograms
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the property of opposite sides in a parallelogram.
questions.question: In a parallelogram, which statement about a pair of opposite sides is always true?
questions.explanation: A parallelogram is defined as a quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel. A key property is that opposite sides are also equal in length. Therefore, a pair of opposite sides is always equal and parallel.
questions.hint: Recall the defining and basic properties of a parallelogram.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate an opposite side length using the equal opposite sides property.
questions.question: In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(AB=8\). What is the length of \(CD\)?
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal. The side \(CD\) is opposite \(AB\), so \(CD=AB=8\).
questions.hint: Use the property that opposite sides of a parallelogram have equal lengths.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate a consecutive angle using the supplementary angle property.
questions.question: In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(\angle A=70^\circ\). What is \(\angle B\)?
questions.explanation:
In a parallelogram, consecutive angles are supplementary. Therefore,
\[
\angle B=180^\circ-\angle A=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ.
\]
questions.hint: Consecutive angles in a parallelogram add to \(180^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: Use the diagonal bisection property to find a segment length.
questions.question: In parallelogram \(ABCD\), diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(O\). If \(AO=5\), what is \(OC\)?
questions.explanation: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Since \(O\) is the midpoint of diagonal \(AC\), we have \(AO=OC\). Given \(AO=5\), it follows that \(OC=5\).
questions.hint: Recall that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

questions.learningObjective: Solve for a variable using the equal opposite angles property.
questions.question: In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(\angle A=3x\) and \(\angle C=120^\circ\). What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so \(\angle A=\angle C\). Thus,
\[
3x=120^\circ.
\]
Dividing both sides by \(3\) gives \(x=40\).
questions.hint: Set the opposite angle expressions equal, then solve for \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve for a variable using the supplementary consecutive angles property.
questions.question: In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(\angle A=(2x+10)^\circ\) and \(\angle B=(3x+20)^\circ\). What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
Consecutive angles in a parallelogram are supplementary, so
\[
(2x+10)+(3x+20)=180.
\]
Simplifying gives \(5x+30=180\), so \(5x=150\). Therefore, \(x=30\).
questions.hint: Set the sum of the two consecutive angles equal to \(180^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: Solve for a variable using the diagonal bisection property.
questions.question: In parallelogram \(ABCD\), diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(O\). If \(AO=2x+3\) and \(OC=11\), what is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so \(AO=OC\). Therefore,
\[
2x+3=11.
\]
Subtracting \(3\) from both sides gives \(2x=8\), so \(x=4\).
questions.hint: Set the two half-diagonal expressions equal, then solve.

questions.learningObjective: Solve for a variable using the equal opposite sides property.
questions.question: In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(AB=3x-2\) and \(CD=10\). What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation:
Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so \(AB=CD\). Thus,
\[
3x-2=10.
\]
Adding \(2\) to both sides gives \(3x=12\), so \(x=4\).
questions.hint: Set the two opposite side expressions equal, then solve for \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the measure of an angle opposite a given angle.
questions.question: In a parallelogram, one angle measures \(65^\circ\). What is the measure of the angle opposite to it?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal. Therefore, the angle opposite the \(65^\circ\) angle also measures \(65^\circ\).
questions.hint: Recall that opposite angles in a parallelogram are equal.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a property of the diagonals of every parallelogram.
questions.question: Which statement is true about the diagonals of every parallelogram?
questions.explanation: In every parallelogram, the diagonals bisect each other. Congruent diagonals are not guaranteed for all parallelograms; that property belongs to rectangles, which are special parallelograms.
questions.hint: Recall which diagonal property is true for all parallelograms, not just rectangles.
